Cache Hierarchy ​

CacheProvider ​

Abstract base class for all cache backends. Both built-in implementations (MemoryCacheProvider, RedisCacheProvider) and any custom subclass share this contract: all operations are async, all values are JSON-serialized, and all keys are transparently prefixed with the provider's rootKey.

typescript
abstract class CacheProvider {
    constructor(config: CacheProviderConfig);

    // Public accessor
    get serviceName(): string;

    // Concrete method — implemented once for all backends
    getOrSet<T>(key: string, factory: () => Promise<T>, ttlSeconds?: number): Promise<T>;

    // Abstract methods — implemented by each backend
    abstract set<T>(key: string, value: T, ttlSeconds?: number): Promise<void>;
    abstract get<T>(key: string): Promise<T | undefined>;
    abstract delete(key: string): Promise<boolean>;
    abstract exists(key: string): Promise<boolean>;
    abstract expire(key: string, ttlSeconds: number): Promise<boolean>;
    abstract ttl(key: string): Promise<number>;
    abstract deletePattern(pattern: string): Promise<number>;
    abstract clear(): Promise<void>;
    abstract health(): Promise<boolean>;
    abstract shutdown(): Promise<void>;

    // Protected — subclass surface
    protected rootKey: string;
    protected _serviceName: string;
    protected defaultTTL: number;
    protected buildKey(key: string): string;
    protected buildPattern(pattern: string): string;
    protected resolveTTL(ttlSeconds?: number): number | undefined;
}

Constructor ​

typescript
constructor(config: CacheProviderConfig)
ParameterTypeRequiredDefaultDescription
configCacheProviderConfigYes—Base configuration; rootKey is validated
config.rootKeystringYes—Non-empty root key prefix for namespace isolation
config.serviceNamestringNo"cache"Service name used for WebAFX service container registration
config.defaultTTLnumberNo0Default TTL in seconds; 0 = no expiry

Throws: Error — "CacheProvider: rootKey is required and cannot be empty" when rootKey is empty or whitespace-only.

Example ​

typescript
import { MemoryCacheProvider } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

interface User {
    id: number;
    name: string;
}

const cache = new MemoryCacheProvider({ rootKey: 'MyApp', defaultTTL: 300 });

// set / get — values are JSON-serialized under the hood
await cache.set<User>('user:123', { id: 123, name: 'Alice' });
const user = await cache.get<User>('user:123');
console.log(user?.name); // 'Alice'

// getOrSet is implemented once in CacheProvider for every backend
const other = await cache.getOrSet<User>('user:456', async () => {
    return { id: 456, name: 'Bob' };
}, 60);
console.log(other.name); // 'Bob'

await cache.shutdown();

MemoryCacheProvider ​

In-memory cache backend with TTL support. Zero external dependencies. Uses a Map store with JSON serialization to match Redis behavior. Expired entries are lazily evicted on access and proactively removed by a periodic cleanup timer.

typescript
class MemoryCacheProvider extends CacheProvider {
    constructor(config: MemoryCacheConfig);
    protected store: Map<string, MemoryCacheEntry>;
    protected cleanupInterval: ReturnType<typeof setInterval> | undefined;
    protected cleanupIntervalMs: number;
    protected patternToRegex(pattern: string): RegExp;
    protected startCleanup(): void;
}

Constructor ​

typescript
constructor(config: MemoryCacheConfig)
ParameterTypeRequiredDefaultDescription
configMemoryCacheConfigYes—Memory cache configuration
config.rootKeystringYes—Root key prefix (non-empty; validated by the base class)
config.serviceNamestringNo"cache"Service name for WebAFX registration
config.defaultTTLnumberNo0Default TTL in seconds; 0 = no expiry
config.cleanupIntervalMsnumberNo60000 (1 min)Cleanup interval for expired entries in milliseconds; <= 0 disables the timer

Throws: Error — "CacheProvider: rootKey is required and cannot be empty" when rootKey is empty or whitespace-only.

The constructor starts the periodic cleanup timer immediately. The timer is unref()'d so it never prevents the Node.js process from exiting.

Methods ​

MethodSignatureReturnsDescription
setset<T>(key: string, value: T, ttlSeconds?: number): Promise<void>Promise<void>JSON-serializes the value and stores it under rootKey:key. TTL is stored as an absolute expiration timestamp (Date.now() + ttl × 1000).
getget<T>(key: string): Promise<T | undefined>Promise<T | undefined>Deserializes the stored JSON. Returns undefined on miss, expiration (lazy eviction), or JSON parse failure.
deletedelete(key: string): Promise<boolean>Promise<boolean>Removes the entry; true when the key existed.
existsexists(key: string): Promise<boolean>Promise<boolean>true when present and not expired; expired entries are evicted on access.
expireexpire(key: string, ttlSeconds: number): Promise<boolean>Promise<boolean>Resets the expiration timestamp; false when the key is missing or already expired.
ttlttl(key: string): Promise<number>Promise<number>Remaining seconds (rounded up to match Redis); -1 = no expiry; -2 = missing/expired.
deletePatterndeletePattern(pattern: string): Promise<number>Promise<number>Converts rootKey:<pattern> (* wildcard) to a regex and deletes every match; returns the deleted count.
clearclear(): Promise<void>Promise<void>Deletes all keys stored under this provider's rootKey prefix only.
healthhealth(): Promise<boolean>Promise<boolean>Always true — no external dependencies to verify.
shutdownshutdown(): Promise<void>Promise<void>Stops the cleanup interval and empties the store.
getOrSetgetOrSet<T>(key: string, factory: () => Promise<T>, ttlSeconds?: number): Promise<T>Promise<T>Cache-aside — inherited from CacheProvider.

Protected Members ​

MemberType / SignatureDescription
storeMap<string, MemoryCacheEntry>Internal storage: prefixed key → serialized value + optional expiresAt timestamp. MemoryCacheEntry is internal and not exported.
cleanupIntervalReturnType<typeof setInterval> | undefinedCleanup timer handle; undefined after shutdown() or when cleanup is disabled
cleanupIntervalMsnumberCleanup interval in milliseconds
patternToRegexprotected patternToRegex(pattern: string): RegExpConverts a glob pattern (* → .*, other regex specials escaped) to an anchored RegExp
startCleanupprotected startCleanup(): voidStarts the periodic expiry sweep; no-op when cleanupIntervalMs <= 0; the interval is unref()'d

Example ​

typescript
import { MemoryCacheProvider } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

const cache = new MemoryCacheProvider({
    rootKey: 'TestApp',
    defaultTTL: 60,
    cleanupIntervalMs: 5000,
});

await cache.set('session:42', { userId: 42, roles: ['admin'] }, 120);
console.log(await cache.ttl('session:42')); // ~120

const deleted = await cache.deletePattern('session:*');
console.log(deleted); // 1

await cache.shutdown();

RedisCacheProvider ​

Redis-backed cache provider using ioredis. All operations map directly to Redis commands (SET ... EX, GET, DEL, EXISTS, EXPIRE, TTL). Pattern operations use SCAN with batched DEL — never KEYS, so the server is never blocked.

typescript
class RedisCacheProvider extends CacheProvider {
    constructor(config: RedisCacheConfig);
    protected client: Redis; // ioredis
    protected scanAndDelete(pattern: string): Promise<number>;
}

Constructor ​

typescript
constructor(config: RedisCacheConfig)
ParameterTypeRequiredDefaultDescription
configRedisCacheConfigYes—Redis cache configuration
config.rootKeystringYes—Root key prefix (non-empty; validated by the base class)
config.serviceNamestringNo"cache"Service name for WebAFX registration
config.defaultTTLnumberNo0Default TTL in seconds; 0 = no expiry
config.hoststringNo"localhost"Redis host
config.portnumberNo6379Redis port
config.passwordstringNo—Redis password
config.dbnumberNo0Redis database index (0–15)
config.urlstringNo—Redis connection URL; takes precedence over host/port/password/db
config.connectTimeoutnumberNo5000Connection timeout in milliseconds
config.maxRetriesPerRequestnumberNo3Maximum number of reconnection attempts

Throws: Error — "CacheProvider: rootKey is required and cannot be empty" when rootKey is empty or whitespace-only.

The ioredis client is created immediately and begins connecting in the background.

Methods ​

MethodSignatureReturnsDescription
setset<T>(key: string, value: T, ttlSeconds?: number): Promise<void>Promise<void>SET with the EX flag when an effective TTL applies; otherwise plain SET. Value is JSON-serialized.
getget<T>(key: string): Promise<T | undefined>Promise<T | undefined>GET, then JSON-parse. Redis null reply → undefined; parse failure → undefined (treated as a miss).
deletedelete(key: string): Promise<boolean>Promise<boolean>DEL; returns true when exactly one key was removed.
existsexists(key: string): Promise<boolean>Promise<boolean>EXISTS; true when the key exists.
expireexpire(key: string, ttlSeconds: number): Promise<boolean>Promise<boolean>EXPIRE; true when the TTL was set on an existing key.
ttlttl(key: string): Promise<number>Promise<number>Raw Redis TTL reply: remaining seconds, -1 (no expiry), -2 (missing key).
deletePatterndeletePattern(pattern: string): Promise<number>Promise<number>SCAN MATCH rootKey:<pattern> COUNT 100 with batched DEL per iteration. Non-blocking, production-safe. Returns total deleted.
clearclear(): Promise<void>Promise<void>SCAN over rootKey:* with batched DEL — namespace-scoped only.
healthhealth(): Promise<boolean>Promise<boolean>PING; true only when the reply is PONG; false on any connection error.
shutdownshutdown(): Promise<void>Promise<void>QUIT — graceful disconnect after pending commands complete.
getOrSetgetOrSet<T>(key: string, factory: () => Promise<T>, ttlSeconds?: number): Promise<T>Promise<T>Cache-aside — inherited from CacheProvider.

Protected Members ​

MemberType / SignatureDescription
clientRedisThe ioredis client instance used for all commands
scanAndDeleteprotected scanAndDelete(pattern: string): Promise<number>SCAN + batched DEL for an already-prefixed pattern; returns the number of keys deleted

Example ​

typescript
import { RedisCacheProvider } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

interface User {
    id: number;
    name: string;
}

const cache = new RedisCacheProvider({
    rootKey: 'MyApp',
    host: 'localhost',
    port: 6379,
    defaultTTL: 300,
});

await cache.set<User>('user:123', { id: 123, name: 'Alice' }, 600);
const user = await cache.get<User>('user:123');
console.log(user?.name); // 'Alice'

await cache.shutdown();

Pub/Sub Hierarchy ​

PubSubProvider ​

Abstract base class for all pub/sub backends. Completely independent from the cache hierarchy. Provides typed, JSON-serialized messaging with transparent channel prefixing; both built-in implementations share this contract.

typescript
abstract class PubSubProvider {
    constructor(config: PubSubProviderConfig);

    // Public accessor
    get serviceName(): string;

    // Abstract methods — implemented by each backend
    abstract publish<T>(channel: string, data: T): Promise<number>;
    abstract subscribe<T = unknown>(channel: string, handler: MessageHandler<T>): Promise<void>;
    abstract unsubscribe(channel: string): Promise<void>;
    abstract psubscribe<T = unknown>(pattern: string, handler: MessageHandler<T>): Promise<void>;
    abstract punsubscribe(pattern: string): Promise<void>;
    abstract activeSubscriptions(): { channels: string[]; patterns: string[] };
    abstract health(): Promise<boolean>;
    abstract shutdown(): Promise<void>;

    // Protected — subclass surface
    protected channelPrefix: string | undefined;
    protected _serviceName: string;
    protected buildChannel(channel: string): string;
    protected buildChannelPattern(pattern: string): string;
    protected stripPrefix(fullChannel: string): string;
    protected safeInvoke<T>(handler: MessageHandler<T>, message: PubSubMessage<T>): Promise<void>;
}

typescript

ParameterTypeRequiredDefaultDescription

config.channelPrefixstringNo—Channel prefix for namespace isolation; when omitted, channels are used as-is

publishpublish<T>(channel: string, data: T): Promise<number>Promise<number>Publishes a JSON-serialized payload; returns the number of subscribers that received the message.
subscribesubscribe<T = unknown>(channel: string, handler: MessageHandler<T>): Promise<void>Promise<void>Subscribes a typed handler to an exact channel. Multiple handlers per channel are allowed.
unsubscribeunsubscribe(channel: string): Promise<void>Promise<void>Removes all handlers for the channel and unsubscribes from the transport.
psubscribepsubscribe<T = unknown>(pattern: string, handler: MessageHandler<T>): Promise<void>Promise<void>Subscribes a typed handler to a glob pattern (* = any sequence, ? = single character).
punsubscribepunsubscribe(pattern: string): Promise<void>Promise<void>Removes all handlers for the pattern and unsubscribes from the transport.
activeSubscriptionsactiveSubscriptions(): { channels: string[]; patterns: string[] }{ channels: string[]; patterns: string[] }Synchronous (not a Promise). Returns user-facing names with the prefix stripped.
healthhealth(): Promise<boolean>Promise<boolean>Backend health check (Redis: PING on both connections; Memory: always true).
shutdownshutdown(): Promise<void>Promise<void>Graceful shutdown — unsubscribes all, closes connections, releases resources.

Protected Members (Subclass Surface) ​

MemberType / SignatureDescription
channelPrefixstring | undefinedChannel prefix; undefined = no prefixing
_serviceNamestringBacking field for the serviceName getter
buildChannelprotected buildChannel(channel: string): stringReturns the prefixed channel, e.g. "MyApp:order:new" (uses CHANNEL_SEPARATOR)
buildChannelPatternprotected buildChannelPattern(pattern: string): stringReturns the prefixed pattern, e.g. "MyApp:order:*"
stripPrefixprotected stripPrefix(fullChannel: string): stringRemoves the channel prefix so handlers always see user-facing names
safeInvokeprotected safeInvoke<T>(handler: MessageHandler<T>, message: PubSubMessage<T>): Promise<void>Invokes a handler inside try/catch; errors are logged via console.error and never break other subscribers

Example ​

typescript
import { MemoryPubSubProvider } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';
import type { PubSubMessage } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

interface OrderEvent {
    orderId: number;
    total: number;
}

const pubsub = new MemoryPubSubProvider({ channelPrefix: 'MyApp' });

await pubsub.subscribe<OrderEvent>('order:new', (msg: PubSubMessage<OrderEvent>) => {
    console.log(`Order ${msg.data.orderId} for $${msg.data.total}`);
});

// Pattern handler receives the same envelope plus the matched pattern
await pubsub.psubscribe('order:*', (msg: PubSubMessage) => {
    console.log(`Matched ${msg.pattern} on ${msg.channel}`);
});

await pubsub.publish('order:new', { orderId: 123, total: 49.99 });

await pubsub.shutdown();

MemoryPubSubProvider ​

In-process pub/sub provider for development and testing. Delivers messages synchronously within the same event loop tick. No network connections; health is always true.

typescript
class MemoryPubSubProvider extends PubSubProvider {
    constructor(config?: MemoryPubSubConfig);
    protected handlers: Map<string, Set<MessageHandler>>;
    protected patternHandlers: Map<string, Set<MessageHandler>>;
    protected matchGlob(channel: string, pattern: string): boolean;
}

Constructor ​

typescript
constructor(config?: MemoryPubSubConfig)
ParameterTypeRequiredDefaultDescription
configMemoryPubSubConfigNo{}Optional configuration
config.channelPrefixstringNo—Channel prefix for namespace isolation
config.serviceNamestringNo"pubsub"Service name for WebAFX registration

Methods ​

MethodSignatureReturnsDescription
publishpublish<T>(channel: string, data: T): Promise<number>Promise<number>Performs a JSON round-trip (handlers receive a fresh copy, no shared references) and delivers to all exact-channel handlers plus matching pattern handlers. Returns the number of local handlers invoked.
subscribesubscribe<T = unknown>(channel: string, handler: MessageHandler<T>): Promise<void>Promise<void>Registers a handler for an exact channel. Multiple handlers per channel; a Set deduplicates identical function references.
unsubscribeunsubscribe(channel: string): Promise<void>Promise<void>Removes all handlers for the channel.
psubscribepsubscribe<T = unknown>(pattern: string, handler: MessageHandler<T>): Promise<void>Promise<void>Registers a glob pattern handler: * matches any sequence, ? matches exactly one character.
punsubscribepunsubscribe(pattern: string): Promise<void>Promise<void>Removes all handlers for the pattern.
activeSubscriptionsactiveSubscriptions(): { channels: string[]; patterns: string[] }{ channels: string[]; patterns: string[] }Synchronous. Exact channels and glob patterns with active handlers.
healthhealth(): Promise<boolean>Promise<boolean>Always true — there are no external connections to verify.
shutdownshutdown(): Promise<void>Promise<void>Clears all channel and pattern handlers.

Protected Members ​

MemberType / SignatureDescription
handlersMap<string, Set<MessageHandler>>Exact channel handlers keyed by user-facing channel name
patternHandlersMap<string, Set<MessageHandler>>Pattern handlers keyed by user-facing pattern
matchGlobprotected matchGlob(channel: string, pattern: string): booleanGlob match converting * → .* and ? → .; all other regex specials are escaped

Example ​

typescript
import { MemoryPubSubProvider } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

const pubsub = new MemoryPubSubProvider({ channelPrefix: 'Test' });

const received: string[] = [];
await pubsub.subscribe<string>('greet', (msg) => {
    received.push(msg.data);
});

await pubsub.publish('greet', 'Hello!');
console.log(received); // ['Hello!'] — memory delivery is synchronous

await pubsub.shutdown();

RedisPubSubProvider ​

Redis-backed pub/sub provider using ioredis. Creates two dedicated connections: a publisher for PUBLISH commands and a subscriber for SUBSCRIBE/PSUBSCRIBE (Redis requires a dedicated connection once a client enters subscriber mode). Multiple in-process handlers for the same channel/pattern share a single Redis subscription.

typescript
class RedisPubSubProvider extends PubSubProvider {
    constructor(config: RedisPubSubConfig);
    protected publisher: Redis;   // ioredis — PUBLISH commands
    protected subscriber: Redis;  // ioredis — SUBSCRIBE/PSUBSCRIBE + message events
    protected handlers: Map<string, Set<MessageHandler>>;
    protected patternHandlers: Map<string, Set<MessageHandler>>;
    protected createRedisClient(config: RedisPubSubConfig): Redis;
    protected setupMessageHandlers(): void;
}

Constructor ​

typescript
constructor(config: RedisPubSubConfig)
ParameterTypeRequiredDefaultDescription
configRedisPubSubConfigYes—Redis pub/sub configuration
config.channelPrefixstringNo—Channel prefix for namespace isolation
config.serviceNamestringNo"pubsub"Service name for WebAFX registration
config.hoststringNo"localhost"Redis host
config.portnumberNo6379Redis port
config.passwordstringNo—Redis password
config.dbnumberNo0Redis database index
config.urlstringNo—Redis connection URL; takes precedence over host/port/password/db
config.connectTimeoutnumberNo5000Connection timeout in milliseconds
config.maxRetriesPerRequestnumberNo3Maximum number of reconnection attempts

Both connections are created immediately, begin connecting in the background, and the subscriber has ioredis message / pmessage listeners wired up for routing.

Methods ​

MethodSignatureReturnsDescription
publishpublish<T>(channel: string, data: T): Promise<number>Promise<number>JSON-serializes the payload and sends PUBLISH on the publisher connection. Returns the number of Redis subscribers that received the message (as reported by Redis — includes subscribers in other processes).
subscribesubscribe<T = unknown>(channel: string, handler: MessageHandler<T>): Promise<void>Promise<void>Registers a local handler; sends SUBSCRIBE on the subscriber connection only on the first handler for that channel.
unsubscribeunsubscribe(channel: string): Promise<void>Promise<void>Sends UNSUBSCRIBE and removes all local handlers for the channel.
psubscribepsubscribe<T = unknown>(pattern: string, handler: MessageHandler<T>): Promise<void>Promise<void>Registers a local pattern handler; sends PSUBSCRIBE only on the first handler for that pattern.
punsubscribepunsubscribe(pattern: string): Promise<void>Promise<void>Sends PUNSUBSCRIBE and removes all local handlers for the pattern.
activeSubscriptionsactiveSubscriptions(): { channels: string[]; patterns: string[] }{ channels: string[]; patterns: string[] }Synchronous. User-facing channel and pattern names (prefix stripped).
healthhealth(): Promise<boolean>Promise<boolean>PING on both connections in parallel; true only when both reply PONG.
shutdownshutdown(): Promise<void>Promise<void>Unsubscribes all channels and patterns, clears handler maps, then QUITs both connections in parallel.

Protected Members ​

MemberType / SignatureDescription
publisherRedisioredis connection used exclusively for PUBLISH
subscriberRedisioredis connection in subscriber mode; source of message / pmessage events
handlersMap<string, Set<MessageHandler>>Exact channel handlers keyed by user-facing channel name
patternHandlersMap<string, Set<MessageHandler>>Pattern handlers keyed by user-facing pattern
createRedisClientprotected createRedisClient(config: RedisPubSubConfig): RedisCreates an ioredis client; honors url precedence over individual connection fields
setupMessageHandlersprotected setupMessageHandlers(): voidWires message/pmessage events: strips the prefix, JSON-parses the payload, and fans out to handlers via safeInvoke

Example ​

typescript
import { RedisPubSubProvider } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';
import type { PubSubMessage } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

interface OrderEvent {
    orderId: number;
    total: number;
}

const pubsub = new RedisPubSubProvider({
    channelPrefix: 'MyApp',
    host: 'localhost',
    port: 6379,
});

await pubsub.subscribe<OrderEvent>('order:new', (msg: PubSubMessage<OrderEvent>) => {
    console.log('New order:', msg.data.orderId);
});
await pubsub.psubscribe('audit:*', (msg: PubSubMessage) => {
    console.log('Audit event:', msg.channel);
});

await pubsub.publish('order:new', { orderId: 123, total: 49.99 });

await pubsub.shutdown();

Cache Plugin Factories ​

All plugin factories return a WebAFX PluginDefinition — the object consumed by app.use(). The package sets:

  • name — the provider's serviceName ("cache" by default, or the configured/custom name).
  • priority — options?.priority ?? 30 (default 30: installs after most core plugins).
  • factory — an async initializer that registers the provider as a singleton service (with dispose calling provider.shutdown()), logs initialization through the WebAFX logger, and returns { health, shutdown } hooks that wire the provider into the WebAFX health endpoint and graceful shutdown.

blendsdk/webafx is an optional peer dependency — it is only needed to feed these PluginDefinitions into a WebAFX application. redisCachePlugin additionally loads the Redis provider; use the ./memory subpath if ioredis must never be evaluated.

createCachePlugin ​

typescript
function createCachePlugin(
    provider: CacheProvider,
    options?: { priority?: number }
): PluginDefinition;
ParameterTypeRequiredDefaultDescription
providerCacheProviderYes—Any cache provider instance: RedisCacheProvider, MemoryCacheProvider, or a custom subclass
options{ priority?: number }No—Optional plugin overrides
options.prioritynumberNo30Plugin installation priority

Returns: PluginDefinition — named after provider.serviceName, priority from options, with a factory that registers the provider as a singleton service and returns health / shutdown hooks.

Example ​

typescript
import { createCachePlugin, MemoryCacheProvider } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

const provider = new MemoryCacheProvider({ rootKey: 'MyApp' });

const plugin = createCachePlugin(provider, { priority: 20 });

console.log(plugin.name);     // 'cache' — from provider.serviceName
console.log(plugin.priority); // 20

await provider.shutdown();

redisCachePlugin ​

typescript
function redisCachePlugin(config: RedisCacheConfig): PluginDefinition;
ParameterTypeRequiredDefaultDescription
configRedisCacheConfigYes—Redis cache configuration — rootKey plus connection options (host, port, password, db, url, connectTimeout, maxRetriesPerRequest), serviceName, defaultTTL

Returns: PluginDefinition. Creates a RedisCacheProvider internally and delegates to createCachePlugin() with default options — the user never instantiates the provider manually.

Example ​

typescript
app.use(redisCachePlugin({
    rootKey: 'MyApp',
    host: 'localhost',
    port: 6379,
    defaultTTL: 300,
}));

Multi-cache with different service names:

typescript
app.use(redisCachePlugin({
    rootKey: 'Sessions',
    host: 'redis-sessions',
    serviceName: 'session-cache',
}));
app.use(redisCachePlugin({
    rootKey: 'Products',
    host: 'redis-products',
    serviceName: 'product-cache',
}));

memoryCachePlugin ​

typescript
function memoryCachePlugin(config: MemoryCacheConfig): PluginDefinition;
ParameterTypeRequiredDefaultDescription
configMemoryCacheConfigYes—Memory cache configuration — rootKey, optional serviceName, defaultTTL, cleanupIntervalMs

Returns: PluginDefinition. Creates a MemoryCacheProvider internally and delegates to createCachePlugin(). Exported from both the main entry and the Redis-free ./memory subpath.

Example ​

typescript
import { memoryCachePlugin } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

const plugin = memoryCachePlugin({ rootKey: 'MyApp', defaultTTL: 300 });

console.log(plugin.name);     // 'cache'
console.log(plugin.priority); // 30

// In a WebAFX application: app.use(plugin)

createCache ​

typescript
function createCache(config: CacheFactoryConfig): CacheProvider;
ParameterTypeRequiredDefaultDescription
configCacheFactoryConfigYes—Factory configuration; the type discriminator selects the backend
config.type"redis" | "memory"Yes—Backend to create
config.rootKeystringYes—Root key prefix for all cache keys
config.serviceNamestringNo"cache"Service name passed through to the provider
config.defaultTTLnumberNo0Default TTL passed through to the provider
config.host / port / password / db / url—No—Redis-only fields; used only when type: "redis"
config.cleanupIntervalMsnumberNo60000Memory-only field; used only when type: "memory"

Returns: CacheProvider — a RedisCacheProvider when type is "redis", a MemoryCacheProvider when type is "memory".

Throws: Error — Unknown cache type: "<type>". Supported types: "redis", "memory". for any other type value.

Example ​

typescript
import { createCache } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

const cache = createCache({
    type: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production' ? 'redis' : 'memory',
    rootKey: 'MyApp',
    host: 'localhost',
    port: 6379,
    defaultTTL: 300,
});

await cache.set('greeting', 'hello');
console.log(await cache.get<string>('greeting')); // 'hello'

await cache.shutdown();

Pub/Sub Plugin Factories ​

These factories return the same PluginDefinition shape as the cache factories, with one addition: pub/sub plugins support declarative subscriptions via options.subscriptions, registered at plugin install time (channel → provider.subscribe(), pattern → provider.psubscribe(), in order). When an entry provides both channel and pattern, the channel branch is used.

createPubSubPlugin ​

typescript
function createPubSubPlugin(
    provider: PubSubProvider,
    options?: PubSubPluginOptions
): PluginDefinition;
ParameterTypeRequiredDefaultDescription
providerPubSubProviderYes—Any pub/sub provider instance: RedisPubSubProvider, MemoryPubSubProvider, or a custom subclass
optionsPubSubPluginOptionsNo—Plugin overrides and declarative subscriptions
options.prioritynumberNo30Plugin installation priority
options.subscriptionsSubscriptionDefinition[]No—Subscriptions registered during the plugin factory execution

Returns: PluginDefinition — named after provider.serviceName, with a factory that registers the provider as a singleton service, registers declarative subscriptions, and returns health / shutdown hooks.

Example ​

typescript
import { createPubSubPlugin, MemoryPubSubProvider } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';
import type { PubSubMessage } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

const provider = new MemoryPubSubProvider({ channelPrefix: 'MyApp' });

const plugin = createPubSubPlugin(provider, {
    subscriptions: [
        {
            channel: 'order:created',
            handler: (msg: PubSubMessage) => console.log(msg.channel, msg.data),
        },
    ],
});

console.log(plugin.name); // 'pubsub'

await provider.shutdown();

redisPubSubPlugin ​

typescript
function redisPubSubPlugin(
    config: RedisPubSubConfig,
    options?: PubSubPluginOptions
): PluginDefinition;
ParameterTypeRequiredDefaultDescription
configRedisPubSubConfigYes—Redis pub/sub configuration — connection options (host, port, password, db, url, connectTimeout, maxRetriesPerRequest), channelPrefix, serviceName
optionsPubSubPluginOptionsNo—Plugin overrides and declarative subscriptions (priority, subscriptions)

Returns: PluginDefinition. Creates a RedisPubSubProvider internally (two connections) and delegates to createPubSubPlugin().

Example ​

typescript
app.use(redisPubSubPlugin(
    { host: 'localhost', port: 6379, channelPrefix: 'MyApp' },
    {
        subscriptions: [
            { channel: 'order:created', handler: handleOrderCreated },
            { pattern: 'audit:*', handler: handleAuditEvent },
        ],
    }
));

memoryPubSubPlugin ​

typescript
function memoryPubSubPlugin(
    config?: MemoryPubSubConfig,
    options?: PubSubPluginOptions
): PluginDefinition;
ParameterTypeRequiredDefaultDescription
configMemoryPubSubConfigNo{}Optional memory pub/sub configuration (channelPrefix, serviceName)
optionsPubSubPluginOptionsNo—Plugin overrides and declarative subscriptions

Returns: PluginDefinition. Creates a MemoryPubSubProvider internally and delegates to createPubSubPlugin(). Exported from both the main entry and the Redis-free ./memory subpath.

Example ​

typescript
import { memoryPubSubPlugin } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';
import type { PubSubMessage } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

const plugin = memoryPubSubPlugin(
    { channelPrefix: 'MyApp' },
    {
        subscriptions: [
            { pattern: 'audit:*', handler: (msg: PubSubMessage) => console.log(msg.channel) },
        ],
    }
);

console.log(plugin.name);     // 'pubsub'
console.log(plugin.priority); // 30

createPubSub ​

typescript
function createPubSub(config: PubSubFactoryConfig): PubSubProvider;
ParameterTypeRequiredDefaultDescription
configPubSubFactoryConfigYes—Factory configuration; the type discriminator selects the backend
config.type"redis" | "memory"Yes—Backend to create
config.channelPrefixstringNo—Channel prefix passed through to the provider
config.serviceNamestringNo"pubsub"Service name passed through to the provider
config.host / password / db / url—No—Redis-only fields; used only when type: "redis"
config.portnumberNo6379Redis-only field; used only when type: "redis"

Example ​

typescript
import { createPubSub } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';
import type { PubSubMessage } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

interface OrderEvent {
    orderId: number;
    total: number;
}

const pubsub = createPubSub({
    type: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production' ? 'redis' : 'memory',
    channelPrefix: 'MyApp',
});

await pubsub.subscribe<OrderEvent>('order:new', (msg: PubSubMessage<OrderEvent>) => {
    console.log('New order:', msg.data.orderId);
});

await pubsub.publish('order:new', { orderId: 1, total: 9.99 });

await pubsub.shutdown();

Configuration Types ​

RedisConnectionConfig ​

Shared Redis connection options used by both RedisCacheConfig and RedisPubSubConfig. When url is provided, it takes precedence over host/port/password/db.

typescript
interface RedisConnectionConfig {
    host?: string;
    port?: number;
    password?: string;
    db?: number;
    url?: string;
    connectTimeout?: number;
    maxRetriesPerRequest?: number;
}
PropertyTypeDescription
hoststringRedis host. Default: "localhost"
portnumberRedis port. Default: 6379
passwordstringRedis password (optional)
dbnumberRedis database index (0–15). Default: 0
urlstringRedis connection URL; overrides host/port/password/db if provided
connectTimeoutnumberConnection timeout in milliseconds. Default: 5000
maxRetriesPerRequestnumberMaximum number of reconnection attempts. Default: 3

CacheProviderConfig ​

Base configuration shared by all cache providers. Every provider requires at minimum a rootKey for namespace isolation.

typescript
interface CacheProviderConfig {
    rootKey: string;
    serviceName?: string;
    defaultTTL?: number;
}
PropertyTypeDescription
rootKeystringRequired. Root key prefix for all cache keys (e.g. "MyApp")
serviceNamestringService name for WebAFX service container registration. Default: "cache"; use different names for multi-cache scenarios
defaultTTLnumberDefault TTL in seconds; 0 means no expiry. Default: 0

RedisCacheConfig ​

Redis cache configuration — extends CacheProviderConfig with RedisConnectionConfig. Exposes the same fields as both bases combined (a non-breaking composition).

typescript
interface RedisCacheConfig extends CacheProviderConfig, RedisConnectionConfig {}
PropertyTypeDescription
rootKeystringRequired. Root key prefix for all cache keys
serviceNamestringService name for WebAFX registration. Default: "cache"
defaultTTLnumberDefault TTL in seconds; 0 = no expiry. Default: 0
host / port / password / db / url / connectTimeout / maxRetriesPerRequest—Redis connection options — see RedisConnectionConfig

MemoryCacheConfig ​

In-memory cache configuration — extends CacheProviderConfig with memory management options.

typescript
interface MemoryCacheConfig extends CacheProviderConfig {
    cleanupIntervalMs?: number;
}
PropertyTypeDescription
rootKeystringRequired. Root key prefix for all cache keys
serviceNamestringService name for WebAFX registration. Default: "cache"
defaultTTLnumberDefault TTL in seconds; 0 = no expiry. Default: 0
cleanupIntervalMsnumberCleanup interval for expired entries in milliseconds. Default: 60000 (1 min); <= 0 disables the cleanup timer

CacheFactoryConfig ​

Configuration for the createCache() environment-based factory. The type field determines the backend; Redis-only fields are used only when type: "redis" and memory-only fields only when type: "memory".

typescript
interface CacheFactoryConfig {
    type: "redis" | "memory";
    rootKey: string;
    serviceName?: string;
    defaultTTL?: number;
    host?: string;
    port?: number;
    password?: string;
    db?: number;
    url?: string;
    cleanupIntervalMs?: number;
}
PropertyTypeDescription
type"redis" | "memory"Required. Cache backend type
rootKeystringRequired. Root key prefix for all cache keys
serviceNamestringService name for WebAFX service container. Default: "cache"
defaultTTLnumberDefault TTL in seconds. Default: 0
hoststringRedis-only: Redis host
portnumberRedis-only: Redis port
passwordstringRedis-only: Redis password
dbnumberRedis-only: Redis database index
urlstringRedis-only: Redis connection URL
cleanupIntervalMsnumberMemory-only: cleanup interval in milliseconds

PubSubProviderConfig ​

Base configuration shared by all pub/sub providers. The channelPrefix provides namespace isolation — all channels are automatically prefixed so multiple applications can share one Redis instance without channel collisions.

typescript
interface PubSubProviderConfig {
    channelPrefix?: string;
    serviceName?: string;
}
PropertyTypeDescription
channelPrefixstringChannel prefix applied to all channels automatically. Example: prefix "MyApp" turns channel "order:new" into "MyApp:order:new"
serviceNamestringService name for WebAFX service container registration. Default: "pubsub"; use different names for multi-pubsub scenarios

RedisPubSubConfig ​

Redis pub/sub configuration — extends PubSubProviderConfig with RedisConnectionConfig. The provider creates two ioredis connections internally: one for publishing and one for subscribing.

typescript
interface RedisPubSubConfig extends PubSubProviderConfig, RedisConnectionConfig {}
PropertyTypeDescription
channelPrefixstringChannel prefix for namespace isolation
serviceNamestringService name for WebAFX registration. Default: "pubsub"
host / port / password / db / url / connectTimeout / maxRetriesPerRequest—Redis connection options — see RedisConnectionConfig

MemoryPubSubConfig ​

In-memory pub/sub configuration — no additional fields beyond the base config.

typescript
interface MemoryPubSubConfig extends PubSubProviderConfig {}
PropertyTypeDescription

serviceNamestringService name for WebAFX registration. Default: "pubsub"

PubSubFactoryConfig ​

Configuration for the createPubSub() environment-based factory. Redis-only fields are used only when type: "redis".

    port?: number;

    db?: number;

}

portnumberRedis-only: Redis port
passwordstringRedis-only: Redis password

Message Types and Plugin Options ​

PubSubMessage ​

Message envelope delivered to subscription handlers. Contains the deserialized payload and metadata about the channel and (for pattern subscriptions) the pattern that matched. The channel field always contains the user-facing name — the prefix is stripped.

typescript
interface PubSubMessage<T = unknown> {
    channel: string;
    data: T;
    pattern?: string;
}
PropertyTypeDescription
channelstringThe channel the message was published to (prefix stripped)
dataTThe deserialized message payload
patternstringFor pattern subscriptions: the pattern that matched (prefix stripped). undefined for exact-channel deliveries

MessageHandler ​

Handler function type for pub/sub messages. Can be synchronous or asynchronous. Errors thrown by handlers are caught and logged (via safeInvoke) — they never break other subscribers or crash the subscriber connection.

typescript
type MessageHandler<T = unknown> = (message: PubSubMessage<T>) => void | Promise<void>;
ParameterTypeDescription
messagePubSubMessage<T>The message envelope with the deserialized payload

Returns: void | Promise<void>

SubscriptionDefinition ​

Subscription entry for declarative registration via plugin options. Exactly one of channel or pattern should be provided: channel subscribes to an exact channel (SUBSCRIBE), pattern subscribes to a glob pattern (PSUBSCRIBE). If both are present, the channel branch is used.

typescript
interface SubscriptionDefinition<T = unknown> {
    channel?: string;
    pattern?: string;
    handler: MessageHandler<T>;
}
PropertyTypeDescription
channelstringExact channel name (mutually exclusive with pattern)
patternstringChannel pattern with glob wildcards (mutually exclusive with channel)
handlerMessageHandler<T>Required. Handler function invoked when a matching message arrives

PubSubPluginOptions ​

Options for createPubSubPlugin(), redisPubSubPlugin(), and memoryPubSubPlugin().

typescript
interface PubSubPluginOptions {
    priority?: number;
    subscriptions?: SubscriptionDefinition[];
}
PropertyTypeDescription
prioritynumberPlugin installation priority. Default: 30
subscriptionsSubscriptionDefinition[]Declarative subscriptions registered at plugin install time. Each entry specifies a channel (exact) or pattern (glob) with a handler; subscriptions are registered in order during the plugin factory execution

Constants ​

ConstantValueDescription
DEFAULT_SERVICE_NAME"cache"Default service name for cache providers and cache plugins when no serviceName is configured
DEFAULT_TTL0Default TTL in seconds; 0 means no expiry
KEY_SEPARATOR":"Separator between rootKey and a user-provided cache key (e.g. "MyApp:user:123")
DEFAULT_PUBSUB_SERVICE_NAME"pubsub"Default service name for pub/sub providers and pub/sub plugins when no serviceName is configured
CHANNEL_SEPARATOR":"Separator between channelPrefix and a channel name (same as KEY_SEPARATOR for consistency)

Memory Subpath (blendsdk/webafx-cache/memory) ​

Redis-free entry point. The main entry point exports the Redis providers, whose modules import ioredis at load time. Applications that only need the in-memory providers — tests, single-instance deployments — can import from this subpath instead, and ioredis is never evaluated.

Exported Values ​

ExportKindNotes
CacheProviderabstract classSame object identity as the main entry
PubSubProviderabstract classSame object identity as the main entry
MemoryCacheProviderclassSame object identity as the main entry
MemoryPubSubProviderclassSame object identity as the main entry
createCachePluginfunctionRedis-free plugin builder — same function as the main entry
createPubSubPluginfunctionRedis-free plugin builder — same function as the main entry
memoryCachePluginfunctionMemory cache plugin factory — see memoryCachePlugin()
memoryPubSubPluginfunctionMemory pub/sub plugin factory — see memoryPubSubPlugin()

Exported Types ​

ExportKind
CacheProviderConfiginterface
MemoryCacheConfiginterface
MemoryPubSubConfiginterface
PubSubPluginOptionsinterface
PubSubMessageinterface
MessageHandlertype alias
SubscriptionDefinitioninterface

The Redis providers (RedisCacheProvider, RedisPubSubProvider) are deliberately not exposed by this subpath.

Example ​

typescript
import { MemoryCacheProvider, memoryCachePlugin } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache/memory';

const cache = new MemoryCacheProvider({ rootKey: 'Edge' });
await cache.set('health', { ok: true });
console.log(await cache.get<{ ok: boolean }>('health')); // { ok: true }
await cache.shutdown();

const plugin = memoryCachePlugin({ rootKey: 'Edge' });
console.log(plugin.name); // 'cache'

Behavioral Notes and Error Semantics ​

BehaviorDetail
Root key validationConstructing any cache provider (CacheProvider, MemoryCacheProvider, RedisCacheProvider) with an empty or whitespace-only rootKey throws Error: "CacheProvider: rootKey is required and cannot be empty". Pub/sub providers do not validate their config.
Unknown factory typescreateCache() throws Unknown cache type: "<type>". Supported types: "redis", "memory".; createPubSub() throws Unknown pub/sub type: "<type>". Supported types: "redis", "memory".
Cache missesget() returns undefined for missing keys, expired entries, and stored values that fail JSON parsing — a corrupt value is treated exactly like a miss.
TTL semanticsEffective TTL is ttlSeconds ?? defaultTTL; an effective TTL of 0 means no expiry. ttl() follows Redis conventions: positive seconds, -1 (no expiry), -2 (missing).
Namespace scopingdeletePattern() and clear() only ever touch keys under the provider's own rootKey prefix — shared Redis databases are safe.
Publish without subscriberspublish() never throws for missing subscribers; it returns 0.
Handler error isolationPub/sub handler errors (sync or async) are caught per handler and logged via console.error; other handlers and the subscriber connection are unaffected.
Fan-out countsMemoryPubSubProvider.publish() returns the number of local handlers invoked (exact + matching pattern handlers). RedisPubSubProvider.publish() returns Redis's subscriber count, which may include subscribers in other processes.
Shared subscriptionsRedisPubSubProvider sends SUBSCRIBE/PSUBSCRIBE only when the first local handler for a channel/pattern is registered; additional local handlers share that single Redis subscription.
Connection lifecycleRedis providers create their ioredis client(s) in the constructor and connect in the background; health() returns false after shutdown() because the connection is closed. MemoryCacheProvider's cleanup timer is unref()'d and never keeps the process alive.

webafx-cache Examples Library ​

This library collects complete, copy-paste ready examples for blendsdk/webafx-cache, organized by feature area. Every example is a self-contained ESM module with full imports — top-level await is used throughout, and expected output is shown as comments. Examples built on the in-memory backends run anywhere with zero infrastructure; examples using Redis assume a reachable server on localhost:6379 (the package's own test suite runs Redis via Docker on port 6399).

Cache Fundamentals ​

Start here: the core caching API with the zero-dependency MemoryCacheProvider. The exact same API — same methods, same semantics — is provided by every backend, so these examples double as a tour of RedisCacheProvider as well.

Creating a Cache and Storing Values ​

Create a cache with a rootKey namespace, store typed values, and read them back. Values are JSON-serialized on write, so cached data is always a safe snapshot with no shared references.

typescript
import { MemoryCacheProvider } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

interface User {
    id: number;
    name: string;
}

const cache = new MemoryCacheProvider({ rootKey: 'MyApp' });

await cache.set<User>('user:123', { id: 123, name: 'Alice' });
await cache.set('counter', 42);
await cache.set('flags', ['beta', 'dark-mode']);

const user = await cache.get<User>('user:123');
console.log(user?.name); // 'Alice'

const counter = await cache.get<number>('counter');
console.log(counter); // 42

const flags = await cache.get<string[]>('flags');
console.log(flags); // [ 'beta', 'dark-mode' ]

// Stored values are snapshots — mutating the original has no effect
const session = { token: 'abc' };
await cache.set('session', session);
session.token = 'changed';
console.log(await cache.get<{ token: string }>('session')); // { token: 'abc' }

await cache.shutdown();

The Cache-Aside Pattern with getOrSet() ​

getOrSet() returns the cached value when it exists and otherwise runs the factory function, caches the result with a TTL, and returns it. On a cache hit the factory is never invoked.

typescript
import { MemoryCacheProvider } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

interface User {
    id: number;
    name: string;
}

const cache = new MemoryCacheProvider({ rootKey: 'MyApp' });

let databaseQueries = 0;

async function loadUserFromDatabase(id: number): Promise<User> {
    databaseQueries++; // stand-in for an expensive query
    return { id, name: 'Alice' };
}

// First call — cache miss: the factory runs and the result is cached for 300 seconds
const first = await cache.getOrSet<User>('user:123', () => loadUserFromDatabase(123), 300);

// Second call — cache hit: the factory is skipped entirely
const second = await cache.getOrSet<User>('user:123', () => loadUserFromDatabase(123), 300);

console.log(first.name);  // 'Alice'
console.log(second.name); // 'Alice'
console.log(databaseQueries); // 1 — the database was queried only once
console.log(await cache.ttl('user:123')); // 300

await cache.shutdown();

Time-to-Live and Expiration ​

Every entry can carry a TTL in seconds. ttl() follows Redis conventions: a positive number is the remaining TTL, -1 means the key exists with no expiry, and -2 means the key does not exist.

typescript
import { MemoryCacheProvider } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

const cache = new MemoryCacheProvider({ rootKey: 'MyApp' });

// Store a verification code that expires in one second
await cache.set('code:8842', '123456', 1);

console.log(await cache.get<string>('code:8842')); // '123456'
console.log(await cache.ttl('code:8842')); // 1 — seconds remaining

// TTL conventions: -1 = exists with no expiry, -2 = does not exist
await cache.set('persistent', 'no-expiry');
console.log(await cache.ttl('persistent')); // -1
console.log(await cache.ttl('missing'));    // -2

// Give the one-second TTL time to lapse
await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 1200));

console.log(await cache.get<string>('code:8842')); // undefined — expired
console.log(await cache.exists('code:8842'));      // false

await cache.shutdown();

Cache Operations ​

The day-to-day operations: removing entries, adjusting TTLs after the fact, invalidating whole key groups, and clearing a namespace.

Deleting Entries and Checking Existence ​

delete() reports whether the key existed (true/false), while exists() performs expiration-aware membership checks.

typescript
import { MemoryCacheProvider } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

const cache = new MemoryCacheProvider({ rootKey: 'MyApp' });

await cache.set('session:abc', { userId: 1 });

console.log(await cache.exists('session:abc')); // true
console.log(await cache.delete('session:abc')); // true — the key existed
console.log(await cache.delete('session:abc')); // false — already gone
console.log(await cache.exists('session:abc')); // false
console.log(await cache.get<string>('session:abc')); // undefined

await cache.shutdown();

Extending or Shortening TTL with expire() ​

expire() updates the TTL of an existing key without touching its value — useful when an operation is still in progress. It returns false when the key does not exist (or has already expired).

typescript
import { MemoryCacheProvider } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

const cache = new MemoryCacheProvider({ rootKey: 'MyApp' });

// A short-lived entry...
await cache.set('upload:token', 'token-value', 60);
console.log(await cache.ttl('upload:token')); // 60

// ...gets extended while the upload is still running
console.log(await cache.expire('upload:token', 600)); // true
console.log(await cache.ttl('upload:token')); // 600

// The same call can shorten a TTL
await cache.expire('upload:token', 30);
console.log(await cache.ttl('upload:token')); // 30

// Keys that do not exist cannot be updated
console.log(await cache.expire('missing', 60)); // false

await cache.shutdown();

Invalidating Groups of Keys with deletePattern() ​

deletePattern() removes every key matching a glob pattern (with * as the wildcard) and returns the number of keys deleted. The pattern can place wildcards anywhere: user:*, *:session, or api:*:active.

typescript
import { MemoryCacheProvider } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

const cache = new MemoryCacheProvider({ rootKey: 'MyApp' });

await cache.set('user:1', { name: 'Alice' });
await cache.set('user:2', { name: 'Bob' });
await cache.set('user:3', { name: 'Carol' });
await cache.set('product:1', { name: 'Widget' });

const deleted = await cache.deletePattern('user:*');

console.log(deleted);                         // 3
console.log(await cache.exists('user:1'));    // false
console.log(await cache.exists('product:1')); // true — untouched

await cache.shutdown();

On the Redis backend this operation is implemented with SCAN plus batched DEL — never the blocking KEYS command — so it is safe to run on production servers.

Clearing a Namespace with clear() ​

clear() removes every key under the provider's rootKey. It is namespace-scoped: it never flushes the entire Redis database and never touches other namespaces.

typescript
import { MemoryCacheProvider } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

const cache = new MemoryCacheProvider({ rootKey: 'MyApp' });

await cache.set('a', 1);
await cache.set('user:1', { name: 'Alice' });
await cache.set('user:2', { name: 'Bob' });

await cache.clear();

console.log(await cache.exists('a'));      // false
console.log(await cache.exists('user:1')); // false
console.log(await cache.exists('user:2')); // false

await cache.shutdown();

Default TTL and Per-Call Overrides ​

A provider-level defaultTTL applies to every set() that does not specify one. An explicit TTL overrides the default, and an explicit 0 disables expiry for that entry.

typescript
import { MemoryCacheProvider } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

const cache = new MemoryCacheProvider({
    rootKey: 'MyApp',
    defaultTTL: 300, // every set() without an explicit TTL lives 5 minutes
});

await cache.set('config', { theme: 'dark' }); // uses defaultTTL
console.log(await cache.ttl('config')); // 300

await cache.set('one-time-token', 'abc', 60); // explicit override
console.log(await cache.ttl('one-time-token')); // 60

await cache.set('permanent', 'value', 0); // 0 overrides the default with "no expiry"
console.log(await cache.ttl('permanent')); // -1

await cache.shutdown();

Namespaces and Multiple Caches ​

Namespacing is how several applications — or several concerns inside one application — share a single backend without key collisions.

Isolating Keys with rootKey ​

Every key is transparently prefixed with the provider's rootKey; user code always works with plain keys. Both clear() and deletePattern() are strictly scoped to one namespace.

typescript
import { MemoryCacheProvider } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

// Two independent namespaces — user code uses the same plain keys in both
const sessions = new MemoryCacheProvider({ rootKey: 'Sessions' });
const products = new MemoryCacheProvider({ rootKey: 'Products' });

await sessions.set('user:1', { token: 'abc123' });
await products.set('user:1', { name: 'Widget' });

// Both entries coexist — the rootKey keeps them apart
console.log(await sessions.get<{ token: string }>('user:1')); // { token: 'abc123' }
console.log(await products.get<{ name: string }>('user:1')); // { name: 'Widget' }

// clear() affects only the calling provider's namespace
await sessions.clear();
console.log(await sessions.exists('user:1')); // false
console.log(await products.exists('user:1')); // true

await sessions.shutdown();
await products.shutdown();

With RedisCacheProvider the same isolation applies on a shared Redis server: the actual Redis keys become Sessions:user:1 and Products:user:1.

Multiple Independent Caches with serviceName ​

When registering caches as WebAFX plugins, the serviceName is the name under which the provider is registered in the service container. Distinct names allow several independent caches in one application.

typescript
import { memoryCachePlugin } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

// Each plugin registers its own singleton service — lookups are by name
const sessionCache = memoryCachePlugin({
    rootKey: 'Sessions',
    serviceName: 'session-cache',
});

const productCache = memoryCachePlugin({
    rootKey: 'Products',
    serviceName: 'product-cache',
});

console.log(sessionCache.name); // 'session-cache'
console.log(productCache.name); // 'product-cache'
console.log(sessionCache.priority); // 30

Inside a WebAFX application:

typescript
import { memoryCachePlugin } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

app.use(memoryCachePlugin({ rootKey: 'Sessions', serviceName: 'session-cache' }));
app.use(memoryCachePlugin({ rootKey: 'Products', serviceName: 'product-cache' }));

Redis-Backed Caching ​

The production backend. Connect to Redis, use the identical cache API, monitor health, and shut down gracefully. These examples require a reachable Redis server and assume localhost:6379.

Connecting to Redis ​

RedisCacheProvider connects via host/port configuration. The client is created immediately and connects in the background — operations await the connection automatically.

typescript
import { RedisCacheProvider } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

interface User {
    id: number;
    name: string;
}

const cache = new RedisCacheProvider({
    rootKey: 'MyApp',
    host: 'localhost',
    port: 6379,
    defaultTTL: 300,
});

await cache.set<User>('user:123', { id: 123, name: 'Alice' });

const user = await cache.get<User>('user:123');
console.log(user?.name); // 'Alice'

// Held in Redis under the namespaced key 'MyApp:user:123'
console.log(await cache.ttl('user:123')); // ~300

await cache.shutdown();

URL-Based Redis Connections ​

Managed Redis providers usually hand you a single connection string. When url is provided it takes precedence over the individual host/port/password/db fields.

typescript
import { RedisCacheProvider } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

const cache = new RedisCacheProvider({
    rootKey: 'MyApp',
    url: 'redis://localhost:6379/1', // URL wins; database index 1
});

await cache.set('greeting', 'hello');
console.log(await cache.get<string>('greeting')); // 'hello'

await cache.shutdown();

Redis Health Checks and Graceful Shutdown ​

health() pings the server and returns false instead of throwing when Redis is unreachable. shutdown() waits for pending commands to finish, then closes the connection.

typescript
import { RedisCacheProvider } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

const cache = new RedisCacheProvider({
    rootKey: 'MyApp',
    host: 'localhost',
    port: 6379,
});

// PING round-trip against the server
console.log(await cache.health()); // true

// Graceful disconnect — waits for in-flight commands
await cache.shutdown();

// The connection is closed now, so health() reports false
console.log(await cache.health()); // false

The WebAFX plugin factory wires both of these into the application automatically: health() feeds the /health endpoint and shutdown() runs during graceful shutdown.

Pub/Sub Fundamentals ​

MemoryPubSubProvider delivers messages in-process with zero infrastructure — ideal for development, tests, and single-instance apps. Messages are JSON round-tripped on publish, so handlers always receive a fresh copy of the payload.

Publishing and Subscribing ​

Subscribe a typed handler to an exact channel and publish a payload to it. publish() resolves with the number of handlers that received the message.

typescript
import { MemoryPubSubProvider } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

interface OrderEvent {
    orderId: number;
    total: number;
}

const pubsub = new MemoryPubSubProvider({ channelPrefix: 'MyApp' });

await pubsub.subscribe<OrderEvent>('order:new', (message) => {
    console.log(`New order #${message.data.orderId} for $${message.data.total}`);
    console.log(`Received on channel: ${message.channel}`);
});

const receivers = await pubsub.publish('order:new', { orderId: 9001, total: 149.5 });

console.log(`Delivered to ${receivers} handler(s)`);

await pubsub.shutdown();

// Output (printed in order):
// New order #9001 for $149.5
// Received on channel: order:new
// Delivered to 1 handler(s)

Note that the handler sees the user-facing channel name (order:new) — the internal channelPrefix (MyApp:) is applied and stripped transparently.

Fan-Out: Multiple Handlers and Receiver Counts ​

Any number of handlers can subscribe to the same channel; each one receives every message. The value returned by publish() counts each delivery.

typescript
import { MemoryPubSubProvider } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

const pubsub = new MemoryPubSubProvider({ channelPrefix: 'MyApp' });

await pubsub.subscribe<{ userId: number }>('user:registered', (message) => {
    console.log(`[welcome-email] user ${message.data.userId}`);
});

await pubsub.subscribe<{ userId: number }>('user:registered', (message) => {
    console.log(`[analytics] user ${message.data.userId}`);
});

await pubsub.subscribe<{ userId: number }>('user:registered', (message) => {
    console.log(`[audit-log] user ${message.data.userId}`);
});

// Resolves with the number of handlers that received the message
const receivers = await pubsub.publish('user:registered', { userId: 42 });
console.log(`[publisher] delivered to ${receivers} handlers`);

await pubsub.shutdown();

// Output (printed in order):
// [welcome-email] user 42
// [analytics] user 42
// [audit-log] user 42
// [publisher] delivered to 3 handlers

Handlers are stored per channel in a Set, so registering the same function reference twice is deduplicated — use distinct functions for distinct reactions.

Pattern Subscriptions with psubscribe() ​

psubscribe() matches channels with glob patterns: * matches any sequence of characters and ? matches exactly one. Pattern-matched messages carry the matching pattern in their envelope.

typescript
import { MemoryPubSubProvider } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

const pubsub = new MemoryPubSubProvider({ channelPrefix: 'MyApp' });

await pubsub.psubscribe<{ id: number }>('order:*', (message) => {
    console.log(`[${message.pattern}] ${message.channel} -> order ${message.data.id}`);
});

// '?' matches exactly one character
await pubsub.psubscribe<{ id: number }>('slot:?', (message) => {
    console.log(`[${message.pattern}] ${message.channel} -> order ${message.data.id}`);
});

await pubsub.publish('order:created', { id: 1 });
await pubsub.publish('order:cancelled', { id: 2 });
await pubsub.publish('slot:a', { id: 3 });
await pubsub.publish('slot:ab', { id: 4 }); // does not match 'slot:?' — no output

await pubsub.shutdown();

// Output (printed in order):
// [order:*] order:created -> order 1
// [order:*] order:cancelled -> order 2
// [slot:?] slot:a -> order 3

A single message can be delivered to exact-channel handlers and every matching pattern handler — each delivery counts toward the value returned by publish().

Managing the Subscription Lifecycle ​

activeSubscriptions() reports the currently registered subscriptions using user-facing (unprefixed) names. unsubscribe() and punsubscribe() remove all handlers for a channel or pattern.

typescript
import { MemoryPubSubProvider } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

const pubsub = new MemoryPubSubProvider({ channelPrefix: 'MyApp' });

await pubsub.subscribe('order:new', () => {
    console.log('[exact] order handler fired');
});
await pubsub.psubscribe('audit:*', () => {
    console.log('[pattern] audit handler fired');
});

await pubsub.publish('order:new', { id: 1 });        // [exact] order handler fired
await pubsub.publish('audit:login', { userId: 1 });  // [pattern] audit handler fired

// activeSubscriptions() returns user-facing names — never the internal prefix
console.log(pubsub.activeSubscriptions());
// { channels: [ 'order:new' ], patterns: [ 'audit:*' ] }

// Remove both subscriptions and verify that nothing is delivered anymore
await pubsub.unsubscribe('order:new');
await pubsub.punsubscribe('audit:*');

console.log(pubsub.activeSubscriptions());
// { channels: [], patterns: [] }

const receivers = await pubsub.publish('order:new', { id: 2 });
console.log(receivers); // 0

await pubsub.shutdown();

Handler Error Isolation ​

A handler that throws — synchronously or as a rejected promise — is caught and logged; every other handler still receives the message, and the failure can never crash the subscriber connection.

typescript
import { MemoryPubSubProvider } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

const pubsub = new MemoryPubSubProvider({ channelPrefix: 'MyApp' });

await pubsub.subscribe('events', () => {
    throw new Error('this handler is broken');
});

await pubsub.subscribe('events', (message) => {
    console.log('healthy handler received:', message.channel); // still fires
});

await pubsub.publish('events', { id: 1 });

await pubsub.shutdown();

// Output (printed in order):
// [PubSub] Handler error on channel "events": this handler is broken
// healthy handler received: events

Redis Pub/Sub ​

The Redis backend adds one crucial capability: messages travel between processes. Each RedisPubSubProvider manages two dedicated connections internally — one for publishing and one for subscribing, as Redis requires a dedicated connection in subscriber mode. These examples require a reachable Redis server.

Redis-Backed Publish/Subscribe ​

Two providers stand in for two application instances sharing one Redis server. A message published by one is delivered to the subscriber on the other.

typescript
import { RedisPubSubProvider } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';
import type { PubSubMessage } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

interface OrderEvent {
    orderId: number;
    total: number;
}

const REDIS = { host: 'localhost', port: 6379, channelPrefix: 'MyApp' };

// Two providers stand in for two app instances sharing one Redis server
const instanceA = new RedisPubSubProvider(REDIS);
const instanceB = new RedisPubSubProvider(REDIS);

let resolveMessage: (message: PubSubMessage<OrderEvent>) => void = () => {};
const received = new Promise<PubSubMessage<OrderEvent>>((resolve) => {
    resolveMessage = resolve;
});

await instanceB.subscribe<OrderEvent>('order:new', (message) => {
    resolveMessage(message);
});

// Give the Redis SUBSCRIBE command a moment to reach the server
await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 100));

// Instance A publishes; instance B's handler fires
await instanceA.publish('order:new', { orderId: 9001, total: 149.5 });

const message = await received;
console.log(message.channel);    // 'order:new'
console.log(message.data.total); // 149.5

await instanceA.shutdown();
await instanceB.shutdown();

Channel Prefix Isolation ​

On a shared Redis server, the channelPrefix isolates services from each other: publishers and subscribers with different prefixes never see each other's messages, even when the channel name is identical.

typescript
import { RedisPubSubProvider } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

const REDIS = { host: 'localhost', port: 6379 };

// Two services sharing one Redis server, isolated by channel prefix
const billing = new RedisPubSubProvider({ ...REDIS, channelPrefix: 'Billing' });
const shipping = new RedisPubSubProvider({ ...REDIS, channelPrefix: 'Shipping' });

const events: string[] = [];

await billing.subscribe('order:paid', () => {
    events.push('billing');
});
await shipping.subscribe('order:paid', () => {
    events.push('shipping');
});

// Give the SUBSCRIBE commands a moment to reach the server
await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 100));

// This goes to 'Billing:order:paid' in Redis — only billing receives it
await billing.publish('order:paid', { orderId: 7 });

// Give the message time to arrive
await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 200));

console.log(events); // [ 'billing' ]

// Subscriptions are reported with unprefixed, user-facing names
console.log(billing.activeSubscriptions());
// { channels: [ 'order:paid' ], patterns: [] }

await billing.shutdown();
await shipping.shutdown();

WebAFX Plugin Integration ​

Plugin factories register a provider as an application-wide singleton service, wire health() into the WebAFX health endpoint, and hook shutdown() into graceful shutdown. The default plugin priority is 30. The app.use(...) calls below are shown as fragments because the app instance comes from blendsdk/webafx.

Registering a Memory Cache Plugin ​

memoryCachePlugin() is the one-liner for the in-memory backend — perfect for development and single-instance deployments.

typescript
import { memoryCachePlugin } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

const plugin = memoryCachePlugin({
    rootKey: 'MyApp',
    defaultTTL: 300,
});

// The plugin registers a singleton 'cache' service, wires health() into
// the /health endpoint, and shutdown() into graceful shutdown.
console.log(plugin.name);     // 'cache'
console.log(plugin.priority); // 30

Inside a WebAFX application:

typescript
import { memoryCachePlugin } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

app.use(memoryCachePlugin({ rootKey: 'MyApp', defaultTTL: 300 }));

Registering a Redis Cache Plugin ​

redisCachePlugin() creates the RedisCacheProvider for you — no manual instantiation needed.

typescript
import { redisCachePlugin } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

const plugin = redisCachePlugin({
    rootKey: 'MyApp',
    host: 'localhost',
    port: 6379,
    defaultTTL: 300,
});

console.log(plugin.name);     // 'cache'
console.log(plugin.priority); // 30

Inside a WebAFX application:

typescript
import { redisCachePlugin } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

app.use(redisCachePlugin({
    rootKey: 'MyApp',
    host: process.env.REDIS_HOST ?? 'localhost',
    port: Number(process.env.REDIS_PORT ?? 6379),
    defaultTTL: 300,
}));

Custom Priority and Reused Providers with createCachePlugin() ​

createCachePlugin() accepts any CacheProvider instance — including a provider you constructed yourself or a custom subclass — and supports overriding the plugin priority.

typescript
import { MemoryCacheProvider, createCachePlugin } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

const cache = new MemoryCacheProvider({
    rootKey: 'MyApp',
    serviceName: 'settings-cache',
});

// The plugin name comes from provider.serviceName; priority is overridable
const plugin = createCachePlugin(cache, { priority: 10 });

console.log(plugin.name);     // 'settings-cache'
console.log(plugin.priority); // 10 — overrides the default of 30

Declarative Pub/Sub Subscriptions ​

memoryPubSubPlugin() (and createPubSubPlugin()) accepts a subscriptions option that registers channel and pattern handlers at plugin installation time — each entry uses either channel (exact) or pattern (glob).

typescript
import { memoryPubSubPlugin } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

const plugin = memoryPubSubPlugin(
    { channelPrefix: 'MyApp', serviceName: 'orders-pubsub' },
    {
        subscriptions: [
            {
                channel: 'order:new',
                handler: (message) => {
                    console.log(
                        `New order event on "${message.channel}":`,
                        JSON.stringify(message.data)
                    );
                },
            },
            {
                pattern: 'audit:*',
                handler: (message) => {
                    console.log(
                        `Audit event on "${message.channel}" (pattern "${message.pattern}")`
                    );
                },
            },
        ],
    }
);

console.log(plugin.name); // 'orders-pubsub'

In declarative handlers, message.data is typed as unknown. When you need the payload strongly typed, register the subscription programmatically instead: provider.subscribe<OrderEvent>('order:new', handler).

Environment-Based Backend Selection ​

createCache() and createPubSub() pick the backend from a type discriminator — the classic pattern is redis in production, memory everywhere else. The same code, the same calls, one configuration switch.

typescript
import { createCache, createPubSub } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

// Pick the backend from the environment — 'redis' in production, 'memory' locally
const backendType = process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production' ? 'redis' : 'memory';

const cache = createCache({
    type: backendType,
    rootKey: 'MyApp',
    defaultTTL: 300,
    // Redis-only fields — ignored when type is 'memory'
    host: process.env.REDIS_HOST ?? 'localhost',
    port: Number(process.env.REDIS_PORT ?? 6379),
});

const pubsub = createPubSub({
    type: backendType,
    channelPrefix: 'MyApp',
    host: process.env.REDIS_HOST ?? 'localhost',
    port: Number(process.env.REDIS_PORT ?? 6379),
});

console.log(cache.constructor.name);  // 'MemoryCacheProvider' (or 'RedisCacheProvider')
console.log(pubsub.constructor.name); // 'MemoryPubSubProvider' (or 'RedisPubSubProvider')

// The returned providers behave identically regardless of the backend
await cache.set('ping', 'pong');
console.log(await cache.get<string>('ping')); // 'pong'

await cache.shutdown();
await pubsub.shutdown();

An unknown type value throws a descriptive error at runtime: Unknown cache type: "postgres". Supported types: "redis", "memory". Register the providers with plugins inside a WebAFX app:

typescript
import { createCachePlugin, createPubSubPlugin } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

app.use(createCachePlugin(cache));
app.use(createPubSubPlugin(pubsub));

Integration Patterns ​

Composing the two hierarchies with application code: backend-agnostic service functions and cache invalidation across instances.

Writing Backend-Agnostic Code ​

Type your service functions against the abstract CacheProvider class and any backend satisfies them — Memory, Redis, or a custom subclass. Swapping backends then requires no code changes at the call sites.

typescript
import { MemoryCacheProvider, type CacheProvider } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

interface User {
    id: number;
    name: string;
}

// Any CacheProvider — Memory, Redis, or custom — satisfies this signature
async function getUser(cache: CacheProvider, id: number): Promise<User> {
    return cache.getOrSet<User>(`user:${id}`, async () => {
        // Stand-in for a database lookup
        return { id, name: 'Alice' };
    }, 300);
}

const cache = new MemoryCacheProvider({ rootKey: 'MyApp' });
const user = await getUser(cache, 123);
console.log(user.name); // 'Alice'

await cache.shutdown();

Passing a RedisCacheProvider — or a provider built by createCache() — to getUser() works without a single change to the function.

Cross-Instance Cache Invalidation via Pub/Sub ​

The classic use of pub/sub alongside a cache: the write path broadcasts an invalidation event, and every instance drops the affected key from its local cache.

typescript
import { MemoryCacheProvider, MemoryPubSubProvider } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

interface Product {
    id: number;
    name: string;
}

const cache = new MemoryCacheProvider({ rootKey: 'Products' });
const pubsub = new MemoryPubSubProvider({ channelPrefix: 'Products' });

// Each instance drops the affected key when a write happens anywhere
await pubsub.subscribe<{ key: string }>('cache:invalidate', async (message) => {
    await cache.delete(message.data.key);
});

// Reads go through the cache-aside pattern
const product = await cache.getOrSet<Product>('product:42', async () => {
    return { id: 42, name: 'Widget' };
}, 300);
console.log(product.name); // 'Widget'

// The write path broadcasts an invalidation after updating the store
await pubsub.publish('cache:invalidate', { key: 'product:42' });

// The subscriber has already evicted the stale entry
console.log(await cache.exists('product:42')); // false

await pubsub.shutdown();
await cache.shutdown();

Replacing both providers with RedisCacheProvider and RedisPubSubProvider (same configuration, same code) turns this into cache coherence across every application instance sharing the Redis server.

Testing and the Redis-Free Subpath ​

The in-memory providers are contract-identical to the Redis backend (the package pins this with cross-backend contract test suites — see 07-testing-strategy.md), which makes them the natural choice for unit tests and infrastructure-free deployments.

Unit Testing Services with Memory Providers ​

Use MemoryCacheProvider in tests: no Docker, no Redis, no cleanup between CI runs. Type the service under test against CacheProvider so the same suite validates behavior that production's Redis backend will provide.

typescript
import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, afterEach } from 'vitest';
import { MemoryCacheProvider, type CacheProvider } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache';

interface User {
    id: number;
    name: string;
}

class UserService {
    constructor(private readonly cache: CacheProvider) {}

    async getUser(id: number): Promise<User> {
        return this.cache.getOrSet<User>(`user:${id}`, async () => {
            // Stand-in for a database query
            return { id, name: 'Alice' };
        }, 60);
    }
}

describe('UserService', () => {
    let cache: MemoryCacheProvider;
    let service: UserService;

    beforeEach(() => {
        cache = new MemoryCacheProvider({
            rootKey: 'Test',
            cleanupIntervalMs: 0, // no background timer during tests
        });
        service = new UserService(cache);
    });

    afterEach(async () => {
        await cache.shutdown();
    });

    it('loads a user on a cold cache', async () => {
        const user = await service.getUser(123);
        expect(user.name).toBe('Alice');
    });

    it('stores the result so the next call hits the cache', async () => {
        await service.getUser(123);
        expect(await cache.exists('user:123')).toBe(true);
    });
});

Importing the Redis-Free Memory Subpath ​

The main entry point loads the Redis providers (and therefore ioredis). Import from blendsdk/webafx-cache/memory instead when you only need the in-memory backends — ioredis is never evaluated.

typescript
import {
    MemoryCacheProvider,
    MemoryPubSubProvider,
    memoryCachePlugin,
    memoryPubSubPlugin,
} from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache/memory';

// ioredis is never loaded when only this subpath is imported
const cache = new MemoryCacheProvider({ rootKey: 'Worker' });
const pubsub = new MemoryPubSubProvider({ channelPrefix: 'Worker' });

await cache.set('job:1', { status: 'queued' });

// Combine both in-memory backends with zero infrastructure
let invalidated = false;
await pubsub.subscribe<{ id: number }>('job:done', async (message) => {
    await cache.delete(`job:${message.data.id}`);
    invalidated = true;
});
await pubsub.publish('job:done', { id: 1 });

console.log(await cache.get<{ status: string }>('job:1')); // undefined — evicted by the event
console.log(invalidated); // true

// The Redis-free plugin factories come from the same entry point
console.log(memoryCachePlugin({ rootKey: 'Worker' }).name); // 'cache'
console.log(memoryPubSubPlugin().name); // 'pubsub'

await pubsub.shutdown();
await cache.shutdown();

The subpath exposes CacheProvider, PubSubProvider, MemoryCacheProvider, MemoryPubSubProvider, the Redis-free builders createCachePlugin / createPubSubPlugin, the memory plugin factories, and the memory/plugin types — deliberately not RedisCacheProvider or RedisPubSubProvider. Every export shares identity with the main entry. Registering the memory plugins inside an app:

typescript
import { memoryCachePlugin, memoryPubSubPlugin } from 'blendsdk/webafx-cache/memory';

app.use(memoryCachePlugin({ rootKey: 'Worker' }));
app.use(memoryPubSubPlugin({ channelPrefix: 'Worker' }));
